summary: The note describes a growing movement to strengthen arts education in K-12 schools through new policies, funding, community partnerships, technology, teacher training, and inclusive curricula. It details dated milestones from September 2023 to March 2024, including the Creative Minds Initiative, a Department of Education and National Endowment for the Arts grant program, the Art Connects program, and the Cultural Expression Act. It closes with a report linking arts programs to better math and science performance and plans for annual arts in education weeks.
one_line: Policies, grants, partnerships, technology, and teacher training are expanding K-12 arts education, with research linking strong art programs to better academic results.
key_facts: As of October 10, 2023, the Creative Minds Initiative, spearheaded by Education Secretary Jane Stevenson, mandates art education integration across all levels of K-12 schooling.
The Creative Minds Initiative includes an allocated budget that lets schools partner with local artists and cultural institutions.
On November 15, 2023, the Department of Education announced a grant program with the National Endowment for the Arts to provide stable financial resources for school arts curricula.
Principal Michael Thompson of Westside Elementary School, an early grant beneficiary, called the grant "a game-changer" and said the school can now plan multi-year projects.
On September 1, 2023, the Rosewood Arts Council initiated "Art Connects," a program partnering public schools in the district with local art galleries and studios.
Art Connects lets students work directly with professional artists and display their creations in public showcases.
Sarah Johnson, an art teacher at Maple Ridge High School, reported artists in residence and student exhibitions in galleries through Art Connects.
The interactive app ArtSpace, launched on December 1, 2023, lets students create and curate virtual art galleries and explore global art archives.
Schools are using digital media, virtual reality, and 3D printing in art education.

On January 20, 2024, the Art Teachers Association led a workshop to train teachers as mentors for aspiring artists; president Emily Rodriguez spoke of nurturing the next generation of creative thinkers.
The Cultural Expression Act, passed February 5, 2024, ensures a broad range of artistic heritages is represented in school curricula, including global art history and indigenous art forms.
A report published March 15, 2024, by the Art Education Research Institute found students in schools with robust art programs performed significantly better in the arts, math, and science.
Nationwide plans are underway for annual arts in education weeks to attract funders, technology partners, and art heavyweights.
